clue.text: Scores badly in acting as substitute but is being deceptive

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the word for standing in for someone

parts.note: an actor doubling plays a part in place of another

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and disordered, so the scores are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An understudy who scores poorly while standing in is secretly up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks like a tally of marks but is just the fodder; doubling is theatre slang for playing a role in someone's place.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross is to betray someone by cheating them, so double-crossing is acting with deceit.

clue.text: Sad record being played has just three notes

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
a record being played is on
three consecutive notes of the sol-fa scale, the fifth spelt in its short form

explanation.surface: A gloomy record whose tune uses only three notes.
explanation.walkthrough: In tonic sol-fa the scale runs do, re, mi, fa, so (or soh), la, te; the clue wants the run so, la, te.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconsolate means downcast and beyond comfort, so it is a stronger synonym for sad.

clue.text: Customary request for a drink

definitions.meaning: second meaning: what a regular asks the barman for, 'the ...'

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the pub regular's order, meaning their regular drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual means habitual or normal, and 'the usual' is a regular's standing order at a bar.

clue.text: Suitor fired one gun — one round initially

parts.note: a fire that has been lit is fired
the Roman numeral for one
gat is old slang for a pistol

indicators.note: the opening letters of the last two words are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of both words

explanation.surface: A wooer shoots a single round from his gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suitor' suggests a lover; here it means someone bringing a suit, a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor in law is one who brings a suit in court, which is what a litigator does.

clue.text: Boasted about daughter being dense

indicators.note: the word for boasted goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: to crow is to boast
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent brags that their daughter is stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dense' reads as stupid, but means packed tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowded place is densely packed with people.

clue.text: Provide too many hands for supervisor

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to staff with more workers than needed
second meaning: a foreman in charge of others

explanation.walkthrough: Hands are workers here, so the first half means overstaffing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to overstaff, and the noun is an old word for a foreman or overseer.

clue.text: Father going to north in alarm

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a male parent
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Dad heading north in a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a device that sounds a loud warning, an alarm.

clue.text: On riotous upheaval and becoming infamous

indicators.note: an upheaval turns everything over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Rioting in an uprising makes someone notorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious and infamous both mean widely known for something bad.

clue.text: Showy performance to daze the first of them

parts.note: to daze is to stun

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A flashy act designed to leave the audience dazed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunt is a feat done chiefly to attract attention, a piece of showmanship.

clue.text: Exaggerate the speed of cricket

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to rate something too highly
second meaning, as two words: the rate at which a side bowls its overs

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, and the over rate is how many overs a team bowls per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Overrating something means valuing it above its worth, which is a form of exaggeration.

clue.text: No longer fashionable cleaner makes smokers cry

parts.note: chimneys give off smoke
to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned cleaning product reduces smokers to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smokers' suggests people with cigarettes; here they are chimneys.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney sweep cleans flues, a trade that faded once coal fires gave way to central heating.

clue.text: Beg idol to be grateful

parts.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A worshipper pleads with an idol out of gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram signal in the clue as printed; the solver has to spot that the seven letters of the first two words rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you are much obliged means you are thankful for a favour done.

clue.text: Sovereign should get on in March

indicators.note: the short word sits inside the name of the month

parts.note: taken as written, split around the inserted word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A king should be on the move in the month of March.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a ruling king or queen, the same as a monarch.

clue.text: Support a good man taking a fixed course

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
a rut is a groove or settled routine one cannot leave

explanation.surface: Backing a virtuous man who sticks to a set path.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a structural brace that holds something up, so it is a support.

clue.text: Pause a little bit when trade is bad

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun: a period of bad trade

parts.note: a recess is a break or pause
an ion is a tiny charged particle

explanation.surface: Business stops for a short while when trading turns poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A recession is a period of economic decline, when commerce shrinks.

clue.text: Like teeth from tined monstrosity

indicators.note: a monstrosity is a misshapen thing, so the letters are deformed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tooth-shaped object fashioned from a hideous pronged creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' reads as a link word, but its letters are part of the anagram with 'tined'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentiform is a technical adjective meaning shaped like a tooth, from Latin dens.

clue.text: Not out on the course but experiencing difficulties

parts.note: the opposite of out
soup is one course of a meal

explanation.surface: A golfer who stays on the course yet is struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not out' and 'course' suggest cricket or golf, but the course is a dish served at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the soup is an idiom for being in serious trouble.

clue.text: Reprimanded severely about rate and rent

indicators.note: the scolding word goes around the word for a charge or speed

parts.note: to lace into someone is to scold them hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenant is told off harshly over the rates and rent owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like the money a tenant pays, but here it is the past tense of rend, meaning torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerated means torn or gashed, and rent as a past participle means torn apart.

clue.text: Sister George initially could be a cat

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A nod to the play The Killing of Sister George, read as a woman who might be catty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is a female tiger, one of the big cats.

clue.text: Settle right afterwards, it's the goal that counts

parts.note: to settle a matter is to decide it
R for right, placed after

explanation.surface: A football pundit noting that only the winning goal matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The decider is the goal that settles a match, the one that determines the winner.

clue.text: Disorderly state? Yes in a sense!

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked whether things are chaotic, someone answers: yes, in a way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorderly state' looks like a definition of chaos, and 'in a sense' like a hedge; the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, alongside sight, hearing, smell and touch.

clue.text: Some of altos singing and drinking

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is taken, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Members of the choir sing and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossing back or tossing off a drink means swallowing it quickly in one go.

clue.text: National flag on hospital

parts.note: a flag is a kind of iris, the yellow flag
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A country's flag flying over a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' suggests a national banner, but here it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue word means belonging to a nation; Irish is one example, of Ireland.

clue.text: Splits Conservative . -holidays

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
leave is time off work, as in shore leave

explanation.surface: Tory party divisions over time off.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray dot and dash in the clue are scanning debris from the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split something apart, as with an axe or cleaver.

clue.text: Give expression to love in sin

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the word for sin

parts.note: a vice is a sin or moral fault
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Confessing a forbidden passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice a feeling is to put it into words and utter it.

clue.text: Interest shared about noon

indicators.note: the word for shared goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: something shared is divided up
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Profits split among investors around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A dividend is a share of profits paid to investors, a return or interest on their holding.

clue.text: Love to be an emblem of peace

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
to be is to exist, or live

explanation.surface: Love wanting to become a symbol of peace.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive branch, carried by the dove in the Noah story, has long symbolised peace.

clue.text: Cheap shape torn apart and rejected as useless

indicators.note: torn apart means ripped into pieces, so the letters are put back together in another order

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A shoddy item ripped up and thrown out as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' looks like part of the anagram signal, but its letters belong to the fodder; 'apart' alone does the signalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the scrap heap has been discarded as no longer of any use.
